html:
The Photian schism was a break between the churches of Rome and Constantinople from 863 to 867. It began when Emperor Michael III deposed the patriarch Ignatius in 858 and put Photios, a learned layman, in his place.

Pope Nicholas I refused to accept the change. He claimed the right to judge the matter as head of the whole church, and in 863 a synod in Rome declared Photios deposed. The quarrel sharpened over who would control the church of newly Christian Bulgaria, whose ruler Boris I was bargaining with both sides. In 867 Photios held a council that excommunicated the pope and condemned Western customs, above all the addition of the Filioque to the creed.

That same year Basil I took power, deposed Photios and restored Ignatius, and a council in 869 and 870 made peace with Rome. Photios later returned as patriarch on better terms. The schism was healed, but its themes, papal power and the Filioque, came back in the schism of 1054.
sum: The Photian schism was a break between the churches of Rome and Constantinople from 863 to 867. It began when Emperor Michael III deposed the patriarch Ignatius in 858 and put Photios, a learned layman, in his place.
